settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The bypassed name maps to the empty placeholder DynamicProxy.class (DynamicProxyMapper.java lines 59-62), not to any class named in the input, so no arbitrary type is instantiated via this path

DynamicProxyConverter.unmarshal resolves interfaces and the handler type through mapper.realClass(...) (DynamicProxyConverter.java lines 108 and 112), which does propagate to the wrapped chain and thus to SecurityMapper when it is in the chain
candidates.description: DynamicProxyMapper.realClass (lines 51-56) compares the incoming element name to its configured alias (default "dynamic-proxy", lines 27/30-33) and, on match, returns DynamicProxy.class directly instead of calling super.realClass / the wrapped chain. SecurityMapper only enforces permissions inside its own realClass (lines 70-77), so any name that is intercepted earlier in the chain never reaches the permission checks. If DynamicProxyMapper is positioned between the stream input and SecurityMapper, requests for the alias bypass type-permission evaluation. The value returned (DynamicProxy.class, line 62, an empty placeholder static class) is not itself an attacker-chosen type, which limits the direct impact; the concern is the general interception pattern that skips SecurityMapper enforcement.
missing_evidence: The construction order of the mapper chain in XStream.java was not readable in this task, so the relative position of DynamicProxyMapper and SecurityMapper is unknown
No reachable flow was shown in which the alias short-circuit yields a security-relevant class rather than the placeholder
preconditions: A security framework (SecurityMapper with restrictive TypePermissions) is configured by the hosting application
The mapper chain places DynamicProxyMapper ahead of SecurityMapper so the alias short-circuit is reached first
Untrusted XML is unmarshalled by that XStream instance
candidates.title: DynamicProxyMapper.realClass returns placeholder class without delegating to the wrapped security mapper

counter_evidence: The handler type is still resolved through mapper.realClass (line 112), i.e. through the mapper chain that includes SecurityMapper when configured
Breaking early means the remaining siblings are not resolved by this loop, so it does not broaden the set of classes that get resolved
candidates.description: In DynamicProxyConverter.unmarshal (lines 104-117), the loop over child elements calls reader.moveDown() at line 105 and reader.moveUp() at line 116. Inside the "handler" branch, when a non-null system class attribute exists, the code assigns handlerType and executes `break` at line 113, skipping the reader.moveUp() at line 116 for that iteration. The subsequent code (lines 121-134) then builds the interfaces array and calls context.convertAnother(proxy, handlerType), then reader.moveUp() at line 128, while the outer loop never resumed the post-break moveUp. This is primarily a stream/reader-state and flow anomaly (potentially affecting subsequent parsing) rather than a demonstrated type-permission bypass, since handlerType is obtained via mapper.realClass (line 112), which traverses the mapper chain toward SecurityMapper.
missing_evidence: No evidence that the skipped moveUp leads to a security-relevant effect (e.g. resolving an otherwise-forbidden type or reaching a different converter) rather than a parsing/state error
Behaviour after the break was not traced through the caller/TreeUnmarshaller
preconditions: Attacker-supplied XML contains a dynamic-proxy structure with a handler element carrying the system class attribute
The XStream instance reaches DynamicProxyConverter.unmarshal for that input
candidates.title: DynamicProxyConverter.unmarshal controls reader positioning via break and bypasses moveUp
